thought.text:
The app finished its build and is serving on 46019. But the port situation has drifted again (each `just serve --apps=X` re-allocates ports for the *running* servers). I've now re-rendered nginx.conf to match the current ports.json {app:46019, cms:36669, boards:32853}.

The robust fix for the memory pressure that keeps killing concurrent dev-server builds is to add swap, then do one clean `just serve` of all three. Let me set that up:

action.command:
swapon --show; df -h / | tail -1
# Add a 4GB swapfile
if [ ! -f /swapfile ]; then
  fallocate -l 4G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap /swapfile > /dev/null && swapon /swapfile && echo "swap added"
else
  echo "swapfile exists"
fi
free -m | sed -n '1,3p'

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments:
{"command": "swapon --show; df -h / | tail -1
# Add a 4GB swapfile
if [ ! -f /swapfile ]; then
  fallocate -l 4G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap /swapfile > /dev/null && swapon /swapfile && echo "swap added"
else
  echo "swapfile exists"
fi
free -m | sed -n '1,3p'", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Add 4GB swapfile for memory headroom"}
